docs.title: Proof notes
docs.text:
This is a small proof-of-concept for mathematical notes that preserve a reader's place. Open the chapter from the left menu, then click an earlier definition or lemma inside the theorem.

Internal references open beside the proof. External sources remain ordinary links.

docs.title: What to try
docs.text:
1. Open Theorem 1.3.
  2. Click Definition 1.1 and Lemma 1.2.
  3. Notice that both references remain open, and neither click moves the page.

docs.title: Even numbers
docs.text:
This short chapter demonstrates the reading interaction intended for longer proof documents.

  1. OpenStax, Elementary Algebra 2e, "The Commutative and Associative Properties". ↩

docs.title: Definition 1.1: Even integers
docs.text:
An integer nnn is even when there is an integer kkk such that n=2kn = 2kn=2k.

The integer kkk is a witness to the claim that nnn is even.

docs.title: Lemma 1.2: Squaring preserves evenness
docs.text:
If nnn is even, then n2n^2n2 is even.

Proof. By Definition 1.1, write n=2kn = 2kn=2k for an integer kkk. Hence

n2=(2k)2=4k2=2(2k2). n^2 = (2k)^2 = 4k^2 = 2(2k^2). n2=(2k)2=4k2=2(2k2).

Since 2k22k^22k2 is an integer, n2n^2n2 is even. □\square□

docs.title: Theorem 1.3: A sum of even squares is even
docs.text:
Let aaa and bbb be even integers. Then a2+b2a^2 + b^2a2+b2 is even.

Proof. The hypothesis means that both aaa and bbb satisfy Definition 1.1. By Lemma 1.2, both a2a^2a2 and b2b^2b2 are even. Thus there are integers r,sr,sr,s for which a2=2ra^2 = 2ra2=2r and b2=2sb^2 = 2sb2=2s. Therefore

a2+b2=2r+2s=2(r+s), a^2 + b^2 = 2r + 2s = 2(r+s), a2+b2=2r+2s=2(r+s),

and r+sr+sr+s is an integer. So a2+b2a^2 + b^2a2+b2 is even. □\square□

The underlying algebra is the distributive law, stated in OpenStax's elementary algebra text.

The proof uses only elementary integer algebra.1
